analysis.title: Commodity Comment: Making Waves
key_insights: Voter anger over high energy prices drove Tuesday's midterm blue wave, but RBC sees a deal ending the Iran war in the near term as challenging. The most likely path for the rest of the year is military escalation or a continued blockade and tanker-attack stalemate.

On a recent Gulf trip, RBC found significant skepticism that a negotiated settlement would fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, since Iran still insists on full implementation of the June MOU. US embassy drawdowns, regional travel advisories and cancelled US participation in major conferences point to a risk of further kinetic action.

RBC sees a divergence between escalation concerns in the Gulf and headline-driven off-ramp optimism among market participants. The pre-midterm selloff assumed the White House would announce a peace deal to stave off a Democratic landslide.

A sustainable agreement becomes more likely if Iran offers major concessions on the nuclear program, cash transfers and Hormuz control rights. Iranian leadership has shown no sign of moderating its demands, and RBC is monitoring the Qatari diplomatic track.
The White House will likely keep the CENTCOM-enforced blockade in place at a minimum. The appeal of an 'escalate to exit' approach could rise now that the electoral imperative has receded.

Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries resumed Oct 30 after a roughly 2-week pause. During the pause, Russian refinery utilization rose to 58% in October from 52% in September, and product exports rose about 180 kb/d m/m with a partial lifting of export constraints.

RBC expects Ukrainian strikes to keep hampering Russian refinery and oil operations and to limit export volumes. Past energy ceasefires have been fleeting, and Ukraine has every incentive to continue while the US has limited leverage.
The midterms add downside risk to RBC's data center gas burn forecast. Candidates who promised data center moratoriums won gubernatorial races in Texas, Ohio and Georgia.

Texas is the most consequential case. Democrats won the whole ballot there, including Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa and a Railroad Commission seat. Air permits for on-site gas plants powering data centers will likely face delays, and Hinojosa could extend Greg Abbott's permit pause.

The nine states whose governor-elect backed a data center pause hold 56.1 GW of planned on-site gas capacity, 45 GW of it in Texas. RBC says the midterms moved the risk to its gas forecasts from upside to downside.

Gold recovered above $4000/oz after the midterms on a weaker dollar and lower yields. RBC attributes this to likely legislative gridlock lowering concern about deficit-increasing legislation, which eases upward pressure on yields and the debasement trade.

RBC expects uncertainty to stay elevated once the new Congress starts, with investigations and Trump focusing on executive action. It sees countervailing forces for gold and 'eyes uncertainty in the coming year'.

Clean energy rallied on the Democratic sweep: the S&P Global Clean Energy Index rose 3% on Nov 4 while the S&P 500 Energy Index fell 4.7%. RBC thinks the optimism may be challenged once Congress reconvenes.

Democratic control may check the administration's efforts to dismantle federal clean energy support, which is most beneficial for offshore wind. Trump still holds veto power and restoring eliminated tax credits would not be easy.
RBC sees permitting reform as the most plausible near-term legislative opportunity, but thinks Democrats are unlikely to concede passage until after the lame duck.
CFTC data as of Oct 27 shows managed money net long gold at 26.6% of futures open interest, versus 25.9% a week earlier. Swap dealers were net short gold at -51.9% of open interest.
Managed money is net short natural gas at -12.3% of open interest (-9.2% a week earlier), and net long crude (Nymex) at only 1.7%.

RBC's oil balance shows a deficit of 5.3 mb/d in Q3 26F and 3.6 mb/d in Q4 26F. Its middle-scenario WTI averages $92 in Q4 26 and $86 for 2026. Middle-scenario Brent averages $96 in Q4 26 and $91 for 2026.
RBC's gold middle scenario is $4370/oz in Q4 26F and $4503 for 2026, falling to $4225 for 2027. Its US natural gas middle scenario is $3.85 in Q4 26F and $3.29 for 2026.

sector_views.rationale: The post-midterm rally reflects hopes for a congressional check on federal rollback, but RBC expects the optimism to be challenged once Congress reconvenes. The president's veto and the difficulty of restoring tax credits limit upside.
Data center moratorium promises and likely permit delays for on-site gas plants, especially in Texas, move the risk to RBC's gas burn forecast from upside to downside.
Renewed Ukrainian strikes are expected to keep Russian refinery runs and export volumes constrained.

tension_points.bull_case: After the midterm rebuke, the President may cut his losses amid public criticism from the America-first camp and Senator Schumer's pledge to end the war, and a deal could follow if Iran offers major concessions on the nuclear program, cash transfers and Hormuz control rights.
tension_points.bear_case: Iranian leadership has shown no sign of moderating its demands, attacks on vessels continue, Gulf contacts are skeptical of a settlement, and the blockade will likely stay in place.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Major Iranian concessions on the nuclear program, cash transfers and Hormuz control rights, possibly via the Qatari diplomatic track, would raise the odds of a sustainable agreement.

tension_points.bull_case: Legislative gridlock lowers concern about deficit-increasing legislation, easing yield pressure and the debasement trade, and weaker dollar and lower yields have lifted gold back above $4000/oz.
tension_points.bear_case: Congressional investigations and Trump's executive action keep uncertainty elevated, and RBC sees countervailing forces for gold in the coming year.

tension_points.bull_case: Democratic control of Congress may check the administration's efforts to dismantle federal clean energy support, which benefits offshore wind.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump retains veto power, restoring eliminated tax credits would not be easy, and Democrats are unlikely to concede permitting reform until after the lame duck.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Permitting reform passing before or after the lame duck would change the near-term legislative picture.
